title: Reduced differentials of a symmetric stabilization
statement: Let $A,B,Q$ be commutative rings with $A$-algebra structures on $B,Q$, let $A_1$ be an $A$-algebra, and let $K$ be an $A_1$-module. Write $S=\operatorname{Sym}_{A_1}(K)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] with a compatible $A$-algebra structure, and $D=S\otimes_A B$. Let $\sigma:B\to Q$, $\eta:A_1\to Q$, and $\tau:D\to Q$ be $A$-algebra maps with $\tau(1\otimes b)=\sigma(b)$ and $\tau(a\otimes1)=\eta(a)$ for $a\in A_1$. Then $Q\otimes_D\Omega_{D/A_1}\cong (Q\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A})\oplus(Q\otimes_{A_1}K)$ as $Q$-modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], where the scalar actions on $Q$ are through $\tau,\sigma,\eta$. No smoothness, projectivity or surjectivity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07M7, first paragraph, symmetric-algebra stabilization; the differential universal-property calculation underlying its conormal direct-sum isomorphism

proof.text: For any Q-module N, restriction of an A1-derivation D→N to the factors gives an A1-derivation S→N and an A-derivation B→N. Conversely (dS,dB) extends by d(s tensor b)=sigma(b) dS(s)+tau(s tensor 1) dB(b). A-balance follows since both derivations kill A; the Leibniz rule follows by expansion on pure tensors. These constructions are inverse since pure tensors generate D.

An A1-derivation S→N is uniquely determined by its A1-linear restriction to K. Given v:K→N, send k to (tau(iota(k) tensor 1),v(k)) in the square-zero Q-algebra Q⊕N and extend by SymmetricAlgebra.lift. Its first component equals the restriction of tau by algHom_ext. Its second component is the required derivation, by the product law (q,n)(qprime,nprime)=(q qprime,q nprime+qprime n). Thus this functor is represented by Q tensor_A1 K.

The B-derivation functor is represented by Q tensor_B Omega[B/A], and the D-derivation functor by Q tensor_D Omega[D/A1]. Combine the inverse restrictions with these differential and tensor universal properties. The inverse of the resulting Q-linear equivalence sends (q tensor db,0) to q tensor d(1 tensor b), and (0,q tensor k) to q tensor d(iota(k) tensor 1). The forward map and inverse agree on these spanning generators by the two restriction formulas. The compatibility equations ensure precisely the stated Q scalar actions.

mathlib_searches.query: Differentials of tensor products of algebras split as the direct sum of the differentials of each factor
Kahler differentials of Sym_A1 K tensor_A B over A1 reduced by a section are the direct sum of reduced differentials of B over A and the reduced module K

theorem symmetric_stabilization_differentials
    (A B Q : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing Q]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A Q] (A₁ : CommAlgCat.{u} A)
    (K : Type u) [AddCommGroup K] [Module A₁ K]
    [Algebra A (SymmetricAlgebra A₁ K)]
    [IsScalarTower A A₁ (SymmetricAlgebra A₁ K)]
    (σ : B →ₐ[A] Q) (η : A₁ →ₐ[A] Q)
    (τ : (SymmetricAlgebra A₁ K ⊗[A] B) →ₐ[A] Q)
    (hσ : τ.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight = σ)
    (hη : ∀ a : A₁, τ (algebraMap A₁ (SymmetricAlgebra A₁ K ⊗[A] B) a) = η a) :
    letI : Algebra B Q := σ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra A₁ Q := η.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra (SymmetricAlgebra A₁ K ⊗[A] B) Q := τ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    Nonempty ((Q ⊗[SymmetricAlgebra A₁ K ⊗[A] B]
      KaehlerDifferential A₁ (SymmetricAlgebra A₁ K ⊗[A] B)) ≃ₗ[Q]
        ((Q ⊗[B] KaehlerDifferential A B) × (Q ⊗[A₁] K)))
